Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 106, verses 1–4:

"O my Lord, make this city a city of peace and provide its people with fruits" (2:126). So Allah made this House a House of peace and kept it free from the domination of dictators and tyrants. Whoever sought refuge in this House found peace, while the nations and individuals around it lived in constant fear. This honour remained with the House even when its inhabitants began to worship idols. They committed shirk, and alongside their Lord they placed idols within the Ka'bah. Allah maintained this honour because He had a purpose to accomplish through this House.

Then, when the People of the Elephant (Ashab al-Fil) resolved to demolish this House, the details of which have passed in Surah al-Fil, Allah protected the peace of this House and preserved its sanctity, while the condition of the people in its surroundings was as it was.

"Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary a secure place, while people are being snatched away from all around them?" (29:67). When the incident of the Elephant occurred, the reverence for the House of Allah grew in the hearts of the Arabs, and this news spread throughout the whole Arabian Peninsula. Similarly, because of this incident, the esteem of the people of Makkah and the custodians of the House of Allah increased, and as a result they moved about throughout Arabia in great peace and security. Wherever they stopped, people showed them consideration and respect. As a consequence, they established two general trade routes for caravans: one running north from Makkah to Syria, and one running south from Makkah to Yemen. The people of Makkah also organised two trading journeys: in the winter season they went on the journey to Yemen, and in the summer season they set out towards Syria.

Despite the fact that the state of peace and security in the surrounding regions of the Arabian Peninsula was not good, with robbery and plunder common everywhere, yet because of the reverence for the House of Allah, these trading journeys of the Quraysh remained secure, and this became a distinguishing feature of the Quraysh. Because of this, wide avenues of livelihood opened before them, and they continued their commercial activities with great tranquillity, peace and safety. Thus the Quraysh became accustomed to these beneficial and profitable journeys, and they could not sit at ease without them.

Just as the incident of the Elephant was presented to them as a favour after the advent of the Prophetic mission, so in this Surah it is stated that it is also a favour of Allah that you have become accustomed to the journeys of winter and summer, and that these journeys bring you great commercial profit. Their region is barren and dry, yet they live within it a very pleasant and prosperous life. This is the bounty of Allah, and it is by this grace and favour that they are secure from fear, whether they are in their homes near the House of Allah or on their journeys; by the honour of this House they are protected from every kind of aggression and oppression.

Allah reminds them of this favour so that they may feel shame and not worship any partners or idols besides Him in this House, because this House belongs to Him; He is the Lord, and it is He who has granted security to this House, within which they live in comfort, and by the name of this House their journeys are kept safe, and they return from their travels safe and sound to their homes.

Thus Allah says: since the Quraysh have become accustomed to the journeys of summer and winter, they should worship only the Lord of this House, who arranged their security during these journeys and made them accustomed to the travel through which they gain material benefits.

"So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger" (106:4). In view of the productivity of their land, their condition should have been that they would die of hunger, but Allah provided them with abundant food and drink, and they ate to their fill.

"And has made them safe from fear" (106:4). In view of their military strength and the society around them, it would have been expected that they would live in constant fear, but Allah transformed their fear into security.

This is a reminder by which shame arises within a person; he feels ashamed and becomes ready to reconsider his conduct. The Quraysh knew the importance of this House and were not unaware of the effects that the reverence for this House had on their lives. It was also a fact that in extremely severe and distressing circumstances they called upon the Lord of this House alone. For example, observe that 'Abd al-Muttalib did not confront Abrahah's army with force, nor did he provide material strength to match Abrahah's power. He appealed to the Lord of this House, who was its true protector and defender. On that occasion 'Abd al-Muttalib turned his attention neither to any idol nor to any deity, nor did he tell Abrahah that the House had many gods who would defend it. Rather, he said: "I am the owner of the camels, and the House has an owner; He Himself will protect it." Yet ignorance (jahiliyyah) is never affected by logic and reality, nor does ignorance accept the truth, nor does it return to reasonable speech.

This Surah, in its theme and atmosphere, is a continuation of Surah al-Fil, although it is an independent Surah, and the Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim is written between the two in the Mushaf. From the revelation order of the Qur'an it is known that nine Surahs were revealed between Surah al-Fil and Surah al-Quraysh, but in the Mushaf they have been joined together because the arrangement of the subject matter and theme has been observed in it.
